source_snapshot.procedure: Verify UART from CPU to USB-C functional.
source_snapshot.criteria: UART is functioning normally and can send and receive traffic over UART.
source_snapshot.bundle: No named bundle; twenty attended and twenty machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; enumerates USB serial devices from the host and assigns the physical send/receive loop to an operator, using an insecure and malformed/truncated SSH example.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly recognizes that enumeration is only a pre-check and physical traffic needs an operator, but descriptor/device-node presence does not prove CPU-UART routing or bidirectional data and the `sshpass` command is unsafe/malformed.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds adapter/path binding, serial parameters, non-sensitive payload, byte/error/timeout criteria, full logs and console-impact protection.

original_test_intent: Prove that the intended CPU UART is physically routed to the specified USB-C connector and can transmit and receive an approved byte stream through the mapped USB-serial adapter or peer without framing, parity, overrun, timeout, disconnect or data-integrity errors.
original_method: Identify the CPU UART controller/channel, USB-C connector and USB-serial adapter/peer by stable topology and descriptors; record baseline console ownership and USB/serial errors; have an operator connect the approved cable/loopback/peer; configure both endpoints with the authorized baud, data bits, parity, stop bits and flow control; exchange a bounded non-sensitive framed payload in both directions; verify exact byte count/order/content, latency/timeouts and error counters; close the port and restore ownership without sending data to an unknown console or retrying automatically.
manual_activity: An operator identifies and photographs the CPU-UART-to-USB-C cable/adapter path and installs the approved loopback or peer; the operator also ensures the selected UART is not an active management or debug console.
required_inputs: CPU UART controller/channel to USB-C connector, cable, adapter and tty/topology map
Supported USB-serial driver and stable VID:PID/serial/path identity
Baud, data bits, parity, stop bits, flow control, direction, payload, repetition, timeout and error acceptance
Loopback/peer setup, console ownership, maintenance approval, cleanup and recovery
safety_requirements: Resolve the exact tty by topology and stable adapter identity; never choose the first `/dev/ttyUSB*` or `/dev/ttyACM*`
Confirm the port is not an active kernel, BMC, service or recovery console before opening or transmitting
Use a bounded non-sensitive payload and explicit timeouts; avoid credentials, escape sequences and uncontrolled echo loops
Preserve full pre/post kernel and serial evidence; do not clear logs or reset USB/controller state merely to retry
Stop on wrong peer, console output/input, disconnect/reset, framing/parity/overrun error or path ambiguity; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate physical/logical mapping, driver, stable adapter identity, serial profile, safe peer and payload
Collect complete descriptors/topology/driver evidence and, after operator confirmation, perform the bounded bidirectional exchange
Verify byte-for-byte content/order/count, timeouts and serial/kernel error deltas, then close and restore the device
Do not use insecure `sshpass`, infer a tty from numbering, send to an unknown console, create an unbounded loop or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CPU UART/USB-C/adapter/tty mapping, peer/loopback and console-ownership exclusion
Approve serial profile, test payload/directions, byte/error/timeout limits and cleanup/recovery
Review physical, topology and bidirectional traffic evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `dmesg` and tty listing are useful discovery inputs but cannot prove the path or traffic; the shown SSH string lacks a separator/space, exposes a password through `sshpass` and truncates evidence with `tail`.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use authenticated access and full, timestamped USB topology/descriptors plus driver logs; then open only the approved stable tty with the exact serial profile and exchange the bounded framed payload with the operator-confirmed loopback/peer.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CPU-to-USB-C UART bidirectional scope and 20/20-minute allocation remain; tty, settings, peer and payload are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: MEDIUM APPROVAL-GATED CPU-UART-TO-USB-C END-TO-END BIDIRECTIONAL TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind CPU UART through connector and adapter to a stable tty, then execute a framed two-direction byte-integrity test with explicit timeout/error counters and console protection.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds stable identity, actual transmit/receive proof, exact serial settings, safe payload, error accounting and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Enumeration can succeed while TX/RX are crossed, one direction is open, the wrong port is selected or the adapter is disconnected from the CPU UART.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Opening or writing the wrong tty can inject input into a privileged console, disrupt recovery access or expose sensitive output.

project_override_considerations: A board-internal UART loopback or fixture may be used only if it exercises the same CPU-to-USB-C path and its topology is documented. Enumeration-only or one-direction evidence is insufficient.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization and CPU-UART/USB-C/adapter/tty topology map
Operator path/connection photo plus full USB descriptors, topology, driver binding and device-node identity
Exact serial profile and timestamped transmitted/received framed payloads in both directions
Byte count/order/content comparison, latency/timeouts and framing/parity/overrun/reset/disconnect counters
Pre/post kernel/USB/serial evidence, console-ownership proof and restored closed state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require functional bidirectional UART traffic from the CPU to USB-C.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The end-to-end UART objective is clear. Mapping, serial profile, physical peer and criteria are supplyable prerequisites.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2166 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00053-V002: approve the CPU UART controller/channel to USB-C connector, adapter and stable tty mapping; loopback/peer and console-ownership exclusion; baud/data/parity/stop/flow settings; bounded payload/directions/repetitions, timeout/error limits, cleanup, and recovery.

review_improvement: Replaces enumeration-only confidence with safe, topology-bound two-direction byte-integrity evidence and prevents traffic from being injected into an unknown console.
independent_technical_reasoning: The criterion explicitly requires both sending and receiving, so a device node or driver line is only prerequisite evidence. USB tty numbering is unstable and may include unrelated management adapters; selection must use stable descriptors and topology tied to the CPU UART. A framed payload in each direction distinguishes swapped/missing TX/RX and detects corruption, while console ownership must be checked because a write to the wrong serial device can affect privileged platform control.
